literal: If you ask what is grace, it is non-killing; killing is the lack of virtue, and eating that flesh is also not a virtuous thing.
translation: If you ask what compassion is, it is the practice of non-killing; killing is the absence of compassion, and eating that flesh is devoid of any virtue.
modern: அருள் என்பது எது என்றால் அது கொல்லாமை ஆகும்; உயிரைக் கொல்லுதல் அருள் இல்லாத தன்மை ஆகும்; அந்த உடலை (ஊனை) உண்பதும் அறம் அல்லாதது ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the essence of compassion as the practice of non-killing. It explains that if one asks what compassion is, the answer is simply not taking any life. Conversely, killing is the very opposite of compassion, and consuming the meat of a killed creature is completely devoid of virtue. The poet emphasizes that one cannot claim to have compassion while participating in the consumption of meat obtained through killing.
